correctness.rationale: For hub bit zero, a fixed hub imposes at most floor(n/2) rim ones. Subdivision-site degree two and original rim-site degree three force y_i=x_i∨x_(i+1) and prohibit rim pattern 101. Conversely these conditions make all sites fixed, so each allowed cyclic word corresponds to one state; color complementation gives factor two. Mark a one-run boundary among r runs and count positive one compositions and zero runs of lengths at least two to derive exactly (n/r) binom(j-1,r-1)binom(n-j-r-1,r-1). The four-state de Bruijn transfer forbids 101 and has det(I-tT)=1-(1+z)t+zt^2-zt^3. Its simple Perron root at z=1 has weighted density μ≈0.411495<1/2, hence a z*>1 exponentially bounds the tail excluded by the hub constraint, giving the claimed asymptotic. Independent bitwise graph simulation n=3..7 gave 8,18,22,44,72; polynomial determinant verified by exact SymPy, not used to replace the proof.
